# Why ice floats

Style: flat. Length: 9 s (270 frames). Rules: the skill's references/story-rules.md.

Logline: A kid wants to sink an ice cube, but it keeps coming back up, until a label tells him why.
Want (visible in frame 1): he holds an ice cube over a glass of water, determined. Hook text: "WILL IT SINK?"
Fact (one true sentence): the same size of ice weighs about 8% less than water (0.9167 vs 0.99987 g/cm3 at 0 C), so ice floats with about 90% of it under the surface.
Source: USGS Water Science School, "Water Density" (water 0.99987 g/cm3 at 0 C; "the density of ice is about 90 percent that of water"); ice 0.9167 g/cm3 at 0 C (Wikipedia, "Ice"). USGS rounds the drop to "about 9 percent"; the exact figure is 8.3%, so the label says 8%.
Structures considered: 1) try, fail, learn  2) myth, then fact ("ice sinks if you push it")  3) zoom reveal (from cube to molecules). Chosen: 1, because the pushing gag gives a real escalation in 9 s.
Loop: he fishes the cube out and holds it up over the glass again; the hook text fades back in, so the last frame is frame 0.
